summary: Outlines an approach for exchanging network reachability information between autonomous systems, an early version of the Border Gateway Protocol. It is experimental. It was replaced by RFC 1163.

eli5.summary: The Internet is made of many separate networks. This is the first way they told each other which places they can reach.

questions: how do autonomous systems exchange routes
how do autonomous systems exchange routing information
how does bgp prevent routing loops
subtitle: The first inter-domain routing protocol for exchanging reachability information between independent networks.

tldr.problem: The Internet consists of many independent networks operated by different organizations. These networks need a way to tell each other which destinations they can reach, and in what order traffic should pass through multiple networks to get there.
tldr.mechanism: BGPv1 establishes reliable TCP connections between routers in different autonomous systems. Routers exchange messages describing which networks they can reach and through which path of intermediate networks, allowing each network to build a graph of inter-network connectivity.
tldr.outcome: The protocol was experimentally deployed and proven workable, but was quickly superseded by RFC 1163, which corrected several issues. BGPv1 demonstrated that a policy-driven, AS-path-based approach was feasible and became the foundation for all subsequent BGP versions.

today: RFC 1105 was replaced by RFC 1163, which is also BGPv1 but with clarifications and corrections. All subsequent BGP implementations use BGPv2, BGPv3, or BGPv4 (RFC 4271), which introduced support for Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR). BGPv1 is not used in modern networks, but the core concepts of AS paths and policy-based routing established by this RFC remain central to Internet routing.

sections.title: Introduction and Design Goals
sections.content:
BGPv1 is an inter-autonomous system routing protocol designed to allow networks operated by different organizations to exchange information about the destinations they can reach. An autonomous system is a network or group of networks operated as a single administrative unit. BGP allows routers at the borders of autonomous systems to determine the best path for traffic destined for networks in other autonomous systems.

The protocol was developed based on experience with EGP (Exterior Gateway Protocol) but with a more flexible approach to policy and path information. Unlike EGP, BGP allows routers to communicate information about the sequence of autonomous systems that traffic must traverse to reach a destination, enabling each AS to apply its own routing policies and avoid routing loops. BGP runs over TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) on port 179, using the reliability and ordered delivery that TCP provides rather than implementing its own fragmentation, retransmission, or sequencing mechanisms.
sections.eli5: BGP helps different networks tell each other where they can send traffic and through which networks the traffic has to pass. It's like railroad networks telling each other 'we go to Chicago, you need to use our tracks to get there.'

sections.title: Message Formats and Protocol Basics
sections.content:
BGPv1 uses five types of messages, all prefixed with a fixed 8-byte header containing a 16-bit marker (all ones for synchronization), a 16-bit length field, an 8-bit version number (1 for BGPv1), an 8-bit type code, and a 16-bit hold timer field. The maximum message size is 1024 bytes; the minimum is 8 bytes (header only). After the header, some messages include additional fields specific to their type. All fields are transmitted in network byte order (big-endian).

The protocol is carefully designed to catch synchronization errors and bad messages. If the marker is not all ones, a synchronization error has occurred and the BGP connection must be closed. If a message is malformed, a NOTIFICATION message is sent with an error code and the malformed data is included, then the connection closes. This strict error handling prevents one peer's corruption from cascading through the network.
sections.eli5: Every message starts with a header that marks where it begins and says how long it is and what kind of message it is. If anything looks wrong, the router says 'error' and closes the connection rather than guessing what went wrong.

sections.title: Message Types and Connection Management
sections.content:
BGPv1 defines five message types. OPEN messages establish a connection, including the sender's autonomous system number, link type (internal, up, down, or horizontal), and authentication code. OPEN CONFIRM acknowledges an OPEN message. UPDATE messages carry routing information, including a gateway address, a sequence of autonomous systems and directions, and a list of networks and their metrics. KEEPALIVE messages are empty except for the header and serve to keep the connection alive. NOTIFICATION messages report errors with a numeric opcode and optional data.

The connection setup process is strict: when a BGP router receives an OPEN message, it validates the link type, verifies that the AS numbers are consistent with the declared link type, and checks authentication. If INTERNAL links are used, both routers must be in the same AS. If both routers are in the same AS but the link is not INTERNAL, that is an error. These checks prevent misconfigurations and ensure the AS graph remains consistent.
sections.eli5: BGP conversations start with routers introducing themselves, saying what network they're in and what kind of relationship they have. Then they swap information about what networks they can reach and what the paths look like. They also send keepalive messages to make sure the connection is still working.

sections.title: Autonomous System Paths and Loop Avoidance
sections.content:
The core of BGPv1 is the UPDATE message, which describes reachability to networks by including the complete path of autonomous systems the traffic must traverse. Each UPDATE specifies a gateway (the advertising router's own address), a sequence of AS numbers with directions for how the route was learned (up, down, horizontal, via EGP, or incomplete), and a list of destination networks. When a router receives an UPDATE, it checks the AS path for loops by verifying that the same AS number does not appear twice in the path.

When a router propagates an UPDATE to a peer in a different AS, it adds its own AS number and link direction to the beginning of the path (unless the link is INTERNAL, in which case the path is passed unmodified). This prepending mechanism allows routers to recognize loops: if an UPDATE returning to a router contains that router's own AS number in the path, a loop has been detected and the route is rejected. This approach allows each AS to apply local policy decisions about which routes to accept and propagate, without requiring a centralized path computation.
sections.eli5: Each network tells its neighbors 'to reach this place, traffic goes through my network, then network A, then network B.' The next router adds itself to the front and passes it on. If a router sees its own name already in the list, it knows the path loops back on itself and rejects it.

sections.title: State Machine and Connection Lifecycle
sections.content:
BGPv1 defines a finite state machine governing router behavior. The machine has five states: Idle (no connection), Active (attempting to open a connection), OpenSent (waiting for an OPEN response), OpenConfirm (waiting for OPEN CONFIRM), and Established (ready to exchange routing information). Specific events—TCP connection success, receipt of OPEN, receipt of OPEN CONFIRM, hold timer expiration, or operator stop commands—trigger transitions between states.

In the Established state, the router can exchange UPDATE, KEEPALIVE, and NOTIFICATION messages. If the hold timer (negotiated during OPEN message exchange) expires without receiving a KEEPALIVE or UPDATE message, the connection closes and the router returns to Idle. Routers are required to send KEEPALIVE messages frequently enough to prevent the hold timer from expiring—a recommended rate is at least one KEEPALIVE per third of the hold time interval.
sections.eli5: A BGP conversation goes through stages: first the routers try to connect, then they introduce themselves, then they wait for confirmation, and finally they can exchange routing information. If one side stops responding, the other waits a bit and then hangs up.
